Luciana, thank you for calling. Did you enjoy visiting our factory in Shenzhen?
Very much, Wei. My team really enjoyed seeing the new cameras in your showroom.
I am happy to hear that. So, what is the next step? Are you ready to place an order?
Not yet. We are considering a pilot in one hospital first. We want to avoid buying a thousand cameras before we test them.
That makes sense. We can send twenty samples next week. What lead time do you need for the pilot?
About two months. Our client can’t afford to wait longer, so please don’t postpone sending the samples.
No problem. And if the pilot goes well, are you planning to order cameras for all four hospitals?
That is the plan. I think you can be a great supplier for us. It is worth trying, and I look forward to working together.
We want to avoid buying before we test the system.

I look forward to working with you.

Hi, I'm Tom, and I help hospital groups choose new suppliers. After a trade show, many buyers come home very excited. They enjoyed meeting new companies, and they want to order immediately. My advice is simple: avoid signing a big contract in the first month. First, ask the supplier to send samples, and test them in your own building. Then, if the samples are good, start with a small pilot. A pilot costs money, of course, but it is worth paying for it, because a bad supplier costs much more. And one more thing: always check the lead time. Some factories promise six weeks and deliver in four months.

Hello Luciana, this is Anjali. I hope you enjoyed traveling with the delegation, and that the jet lag is gone. I am calling for two reasons. First, I would like to thank you for being such a great group. Several hosts asked me to tell you that they enjoyed meeting your team. Second, I need to collect some feedback about the trip. Could you spend ten minutes answering a short survey this week? We are planning to organize another trip in April, to a trade show in Shanghai, and your answers will help us improve it. If your team is interested in joining us, please let me know before the end of the month.

Luciana, it's Giulia. I read the pilot agreement from Wei's company. In general, it looks good, but I suggest changing two points before you sign. First, the agreement says that Teleinfo agrees to buy the cameras for all four hospitals after the pilot. I recommend removing that sentence. You want to keep the option of choosing another supplier if the test fails. Second, there is no date for the samples. Ask them to promise a delivery date in writing. I know you don't want to postpone the project, but it is worth waiting two or three days to get this right. I can send you my comments tomorrow.
